summaryBox.takeaway: Cardiovascular center in Medulla Oblongata: Sympathetic nerves (Noradrenaline) increase HR/CO; Parasympathetic (Vagus, Acetylcholine) decreases HR. CAD/Atherosclerosis narrows arteries; Infarction is muscle death; Heart failure is reduced pumping.

NEURO-ENDOCRINE CARDIA CONTROL
                                     │
         ┌───────────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                       ▼
  AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM (ANS)                           ENDOCRINE HORMONES
  Center: **Medulla Oblongata**                           ├── Adrenal Medullary Hormones:
  ├── Sympathetic Nerves (Noradrenaline)                  │   **Adrenaline & Noradrenaline**
  │   ──► INCREASES HR, SV, and Cardiac Output            │   ──► Increases HR, contractility, & CO
  └── Parasympathetic / Vagus Nerve (Acetylcholine)       └── Thyroxine ($\text{T}_4$):
      ──► DECREASES HR, conduction, & CO                       ──► Increases heart rate & sensitivity
conceptBreakdown.content:
Cardiac activity is regulated intrinsically by nodal tissue (**Myogenic Autorhythmicity**), but modified by neural and endocrine systems.

### 9.1 Pathophysiology of Cardiovascular Disorders

| Circulatory Disorder | Etiology & Pathological Mechanism | Clinical & Diagnostic Manifestations |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hypertension (High Blood Pressure)** | Persistent elevation of systemic arterial blood pressure above normal physiological levels ($>140/90\text{ mmHg}$) | Systolic $>140\text{ mmHg}$ or Diastolic $>90\text{ mmHg}$ ($120/80$ is normal). Leads to heart disease, renal damage, and stroke |
| **Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) / Atherosclerosis** | Deposition of **calcium, fat, cholesterol, and fibrous tissue** in the tunica intima of coronary arteries | Narrows arterial lumen, restricting blood flow to the myocardium; main cause of ischemia |
| **Angina Pectoris** | Transient myocardial ischemia resulting from inadequate blood flow through stenotic coronary arteries | Acute, crushing substernal chest pain radiating to left arm; triggered by exertion, relieved by rest or nitroglycerin |
| **Myocardial Infarction (Heart Attack)** | Sudden ischemic necrosis/death of a region of myocardium due to complete thrombotic occlusion of a coronary artery | Severe, persistent chest pain, elevated cardiac troponins ($\text{cTnT / cTnI}$), and **ST-segment elevation** on ECG |
| **Heart Failure (Congestive)** | Inability of the heart to pump blood effectively to meet metabolic demands of tissues | Main symptom is **lung congestion** (pulmonary edema) in left-sided failure; peripheral edema in right-sided failure |
| **Cardiac Arrest** | Complete cessation of cardiac electrical and mechanical activity | Heart stops beating entirely; zero cardiac output; loss of consciousness |
